sections.name: Two Guards, Two Doors
lines: N
You're locked in a dungeon with two doors. One leads to freedom. The other leads to a hungry beast.
You're locked in a dungeon with two doors. One leads to freedom. The other leads to a hungry beast.
N
Each door has a guard. One always tells the truth. The other always lies. You do not know which is which.
Each door has a guard. One always tells the truth. The other always lies. You don't know which is which.
N
You may ask only one question, to only one guard.

N

lines.ask: What one question gets you out?

lines: What one question gets you out? You have 10 seconds. Think!
What one question gets you out? You have 10 seconds. Think!
N

lines.answer: Ask: which door would the|OTHER guard say is freedom?|Then take the opposite door.

lines: Ask either guard: which door would the other guard say leads to freedom? Then take the opposite door.
Ask either guard: which door would the other guard say leads to freedom? Then take the opposite door.
N
The truthful guard reports the liar's wrong answer. The liar twists the truthful one's answer. Either way, you hear the wrong door.
